q1.boundary: The Catalog Management bounded context (catalog-management) becomes the broker boundary: its two services move from Redpanda to Apache Kafka, while every other service (ecommerce-product-query-service, ecommerce-category-query-service, ecommerce-tenant-service and the rest) stays on Redpanda. Every consumer x topic binding that crosses catalog-management (INBOUND or OUTBOUND) therefore now also crosses the Redpanda/Kafka boundary and must be carried by MirrorMaker 2. Bindings inside the context (image-service on catalog.product.events) move together with it.

q4.must_preserve: Both producers of this topic move (catalog-service: ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted; image-service: ProductImagePromoted), so every record they write on Kafka must be mirrored into the same-named topic on Redpanda, keeping key, partition, per-key order and headers (tenant header), so the product read model and image URLs on the storefront keep updating.

q5.statement: The list of bindings may be incomplete: the AIP capture covers only its configured consumer groups at one capture time (2026-10-29T20:02:22Z). A consumer group not in the capture (another team's service, a tool, a renamed group) would not appear. The execution session must compare the live Redpanda group list (platform team, P00) with q2 before starting.

An attachment shows only that a group is assigned to a topic, not that it handles the events. Whether product-query and category-query actually process attribute events, and whether product-query also needs catalog.category.events (no attachment seen; its repository is not in the workspace), is not established. The allow-list mirrors all three catalog topics regardless, so this does not change the plan.

Producers are declared only. That catalog-service and image-service are the only producers of the three catalog topics, and tenant-service the only producer of tenant.tenant.events, comes from source and the catalog, not from the broker. If another producer writes to a catalog topic on Redpanda after the move, those records would not reach the moved image-service.

Delivery between the brokers is not established by any evidence I have; MM2 is at-least-once. The move is not claimed to be lossless or exactly-once. Duplicates can occur (MM2 restarts, offset translation, rollback), and records written to Redpanda's catalog.product.events but not yet read by image-service at cutover would be missed if the drain check (P04) is skipped.

evidence.reference: Binding picture: delivery between brokers is never established
MirrorMaker 2 provides at-least-once replication; offset translation is approximate.

q5.statement: The exact Helm values files and keys for the broker address, and the group ids used locally, are not visible: the values repository is not in the workspace. AIP shows catalog-service's tenant group as ecommerce-catalog-service, while config.e2e.yaml uses catalog-service-tenant-events; the live group ids must be confirmed before the MM2 groups allow-list is set.

To verify after the move: (1) on Kafka, both moved groups are attached to tenant.tenant.events and image-service to catalog.product.events; (2) on Redpanda, product-query and category-query groups keep consuming new records on all three catalog topics with lag returning to 0; (3) mirrored records keep key, partition and the tenant header; (4) the functional test passes (requested from the operator); (5) Redpanda shows no catalog-service/image-service group members left; (6) a fresh AIP binding picture, taken after the move, shows the moved bindings on the Kafka broker.

evidence.reference: These are the checks P07 and P08 of plan.json; each is a stop condition.
